science.qualification: Uniform photosphere color from the star's ESO VLT/X-shooter wide-slit spectrum, dimmed toward the limb by the quadratic V-band law Claret & Bloemen (2011) compute from ATLAS model atmospheres, interpolated to the star's temperature and gravity: a model, because no image measures this star's limb. The disc is unresolved: no map or absolute brightness is implied. Self-luminous, so no lighting.

science.label: Sector 11
science.description: Brightness of the star's surface that reproduces its light as it turns once in 3.06 days, fitted with starry to the TESS mission's own 2-minute light curve of sector 11 (its PDC-MAP flux) (the light varies by 14%; the map's curve leaves a scatter of 2.0%, the light's own noise being 0.26%). A light curve fixes how bright each longitude is, not the latitude of what darkens it. In this sector the method of Holcomb et al. (2022, ApJ 936, 138) finds a period of 3.04 d from the autocorrelation, whose peaks have a height of 0.33, a width of 0.48 and a fit of 1.00, and in all 3 of the star's sectors together a period of 3.06 d from the autocorrelation, whose peaks have a height of 0.25, a width of 0.48 and a fit of 0.99; its criteria accept that as the star's rotation. The map is made at a tilt of 55°, worked out from the star's rotation speed, period and radius. Gaia DR3 lists 28 other stars within 63 arcseconds, with 8.0% of their light and the star's together. A reduction made in this project, not a published map.
science.title: TESS · brightness map made here · Sector 11

science.label: Color + brightness
science.description: The star's color (#ffcb9b, its Color dataset) over the brightness map this project made from the star's light in TESS sector 102 (March and April 2026): the map's scale, 50% to 150% of the mean surface, runs from a darker, richer tone of the same hue to the color itself. The contrast is drawn far stronger than it is, so the parts can be told apart: the darkest part gives 60.4% less light than the brightest. Longitudes are fixed by the light curve; latitudes and shapes are not. No color change of the spots is drawn: none is measured. A reduction made in this project, not a published map.
science.title: TESS · the star in its color over its brightness map · March and April 2026
